1.label: Beginner
1.tenses: present tense only (plus fixed polite phrases like 'vorrei')
1.notes: Speak slowly and simply. After each Italian reply, it's OK to add a very short English gloss of hard words. Gently offer two choices to answer from when the learner seems stuck.

2.label: Elementary
2.tenses: present, passato prossimo, and modal verbs (volere, potere, dovere); avoid the subjunctive
2.notes: Use English only for a single tricky word, and only if the learner seems lost. Ask follow-up questions that make the learner talk about the past.

3.label: Conversational
3.tenses: natural spoken Italian: present, passato prossimo, imperfetto, future, conditional (vorrei, potrei); occasional common subjunctive in fixed phrases is fine
3.notes: Natural speed and register. No English unless the learner explicitly asks. Occasionally say something the learner may not understand, so they practice 'può ripetere?' and 'come si dice…?'.

grammar: Italian pronunciation (c/g/sc, double consonants, gli, gn)
essere: io sono, tu sei, lui/lei è
Formal Lei vs. informal tu
weeks.goal: Say hello, your name, where you're from, and that you're learning Italian.

grammar: Definite and indefinite articles (il/lo/la/l'/i/gli/le, un/uno/una/un')
Noun gender and plurals
avere: ho, hai, ha; 'ho fame', 'ho 35 anni'
weeks.goal: Order coffee and a simple meal; say what you like and don't like.

grammar: Regular present tense: -are, -ere, -ire (parlo, prendo, dormo, capisco)
Numbers, prices, and telling time
Question words: dove, quando, quanto, come, perché
weeks.goal: Talk about your day in the present tense; handle prices and times.

grammar: andare, fare, venire, stare, uscire (present)
volere, potere, dovere + infinitive
Prepositions with articles (al, del, nel, sul)
weeks.goal: Buy a train ticket and ask for directions without English.

grammar: Passato prossimo with avere (ho mangiato, ho fatto)
Passato prossimo with essere (sono andato/a)
Common irregular past participles (fatto, detto, visto, preso, stato)
weeks.goal: Tell someone what you did last weekend.

grammar: Reflexive verbs (mi sveglio, mi chiamo)
Frequency words (sempre, spesso, mai)
Direct object pronouns (lo, la, li, le)
weeks.goal: Describe your job as a software engineer and your daily routine.

grammar: Simple future (andrò, farò, sarò)
Conditional for politeness: vorrei, potrei, mi piacerebbe
Making plans: 'pensavo di…', 'ho intenzione di…'
weeks.goal: Talk about your summer trip plans and make polite requests.

grammar: Opinions: secondo me, penso che, mi sembra
Connectors: però, quindi, allora, invece, comunque, infatti
Comparisons: più… di, meno… di, come
weeks.goal: Give and defend a simple opinion; keep a conversation going for 15 minutes.

grammar: Repair strategies: può ripetere?, come si dice…?, cosa vuol dire…?
Describing problems: non funziona, ho perso…, mi fa male…
Review: passato prossimo vs. present vs. future
weeks.goal: Get through a 20 to 30 minute conversation and solve a travel problem.

introductions.label: Introducing myself
introductions.role: a friendly Italian person (Giulia, 30s, from Bologna) meeting the learner at a language exchange evening
introductions.goal: Get to know the learner: name, where they're from, family, why they're learning Italian.
introductions.opening: Greet the learner warmly and ask their name.

job.label: Talking about my job
job.role: Marco, an Italian product manager at a tech meetup in Milan, curious about the learner's work as a software engineer
job.goal: Ask about the learner's job, company, what they build, working from home, and their new job starting in January.
job.opening: Introduce yourself briefly and ask what the learner does for work.

restaurant.label: Ordering at a restaurant
restaurant.role: a waiter at a trattoria in Florence
restaurant.goal: Seat the learner, take a drink order, recommend a dish, take the food order, handle a question or allergy, and bring the check.
restaurant.opening: Greet the learner at the door and ask how many people.

hotel.label: Checking into a hotel
hotel.role: a receptionist at a small hotel in Rome
hotel.goal: Check the learner in: reservation name, ID, breakfast time, Wi-Fi, and one small problem (the room isn't ready yet, or the air conditioning is broken).
hotel.opening: Greet the learner at the front desk.

train_tickets.label: Buying train tickets
train_tickets.role: a ticket agent at Roma Termini station
train_tickets.goal: Sell the learner a ticket: destination, one-way or round trip, time, class, price, platform, and a delay or a change of trains.
train_tickets.opening: Call the learner to the window and ask how you can help.

directions.label: Asking for directions
directions.role: a helpful local walking a dog in Naples
directions.goal: Help the learner find a place (the station, a museum, a pharmacy). Give directions with a destra, a sinistra, dritto, and landmarks; check they understood.
directions.opening: React to the learner saying 'scusi' on the street.

shopping.label: Shopping
shopping.role: a shop assistant in a clothing store in Milan
shopping.goal: Help the learner find a size and color, try something on, discuss price, and pay.
shopping.opening: Greet the learner as they enter the shop.

pharmacy.label: At the pharmacy
pharmacy.goal: Ask about symptoms, how long, allergies; recommend something; explain how often to take it.
pharmacy.opening: Greet the learner and ask what they need.

small_talk.label: Small talk with a stranger
small_talk.role: a chatty older Italian (Signor Rossi) sitting next to the learner on a train
small_talk.goal: Chat about where the learner is going, the weather, family, food, and Italy vs. America.
small_talk.opening: Make a friendly comment and ask where the learner is headed.

free.label: Free conversation
free.role: a friendly Italian conversation partner (Luca, from Turin)
free.goal: Have a natural conversation about whatever the learner wants: plans, hobbies, opinions, the trip to Italy next summer. Keep it going with follow-up questions.
free.opening: Greet the learner and ask how their day is going.
